key_insight: SearchOS-V1 introduces a system-level multi-agent search framework designed to keep information-seeking agents on track during long web-search tasks. Its core value is reducing repetitive failure loops so agents can use search budgets more effectively and produce more complete answers.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a common failure mode in tool-integrated LLM agents: as search histories grow, agents lose task awareness, repeat unhelpful actions, and get stuck in loops when evidence is hard to find. This wastes search budget and lowers final answer quality and completeness.
method: Builds a collaborative multi-agent search system for open-domain information seeking.
Adds mechanisms to monitor task progress and prevent agents from repeatedly exploring the same unproductive paths.
Improves robustness when web searches fail by coordinating agent behavior instead of relying on a single agent’s local search history.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SearchOS-V1 points to a practical way to make search agents more reliable in real-world, long-horizon retrieval tasks. It is especially relevant for systems that need sustained web exploration, fewer wasted tool calls, and stronger end-to-end answer quality.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multiple agents collaborating across search, evidence collection, and answer synthesis.

paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
paper_authors: Yuyao Zhang, Junjie Gao, Zhengxian Wu, Jiaming Fan, Jin Zhang
